text:
Jess: quick question — onboarding sampleapp still showing duplicate side-effects when we hit 429 and token refresh kicks in. anyone seen this pattern?
Hao: saw a repro yesterday, yeah. sequence: client hits 429, token refresh, SDK retries without idempotency key so server treats it as a new attempt.
Sam: is the retry happening inside our SDK or the sampleapp wrapper?
Jess: inside SDK for the sampleapp default config. default backoff is exponential w/o jitter in the sample.
Margo: ugh. exponential without jitter + token rotation window = thundering replays.
Hao: attaching the minimal log I used:
```
[2026-03-15T12:01:02Z] POST /v1/generate -> 429
[2026-03-15T12:01:02Z] token refresh start
[2026-03-15T12:01:03Z] retry attempt 1 -> POST /v1/generate (no idempotency header)
[2026-03-15T12:01:03Z] server accepted -> duplicate side-effect
```
Sam: ok, two things: 1) SDK should attach an idempotency token by default for mutating endpoints. 2) backoff should include jitter.
Jess: agreed. adding default idempotency header `Idempotency-Key` probably fine. but worried about long-lived streaming requests — does that break resume logic?
Margo: for streaming, idempotency is trickier. resumable streams need separate resume tokens; idempotency-key mainly for short RPCs. sampleapp uses non-streaming generation so fine.
Hao: suggestion: default retry policy = full-jitter (per AWS backoff paper) + max-retries 4 for 429, and always preserve user-provided idempotency header if present.
Sam: full-jitter example:
```
base = 100ms
cap = 2s
sleep = random_between(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt))
```
Jess: can we also add a small grace window for token rotation? e.g., SDK tags retries with the pre-refresh token id so server can detect replay if refresh happened?
Margo: we already send Authorization header which changes after refresh. tagging retries with `X-RW-Token-Snapshot` would be weird. better to rely on idempotency key.
Hao: agreed. but we can also make the SDK preserve in-flight request metadata across refresh so that the retry uses same idempotency key.
Sam: test plan: add unit that simulates 429 before and after token refresh and assert server receives same idempotency-key value. integration: sampleapp harness with flaky auth endpoint.
Jess: who wants to own the SDK change? small patch in node + python parity needed.
Hao: I can do Node side, will add full-jitter util and default header.
Margo: I’ll pick up Python parity and the sampleapp update.
Jess: awesome. pls add a note in onboarding README about idempotency expectations so customers know we default it for mutating routes.
Sam: also: add a quick e2e flakiness test to our CI that simulates 429+auth-rotate for sampleapp — helps catch regressions.
deploy-bot: scheduled job created: `ci/onboarding/429-auth-rotate` (weekly) :white_check_mark:
Jess: thx. small follow-up: should we expose the jitter strategy via SDK config or keep opinionated default?
Hao: expose as opt-in; default = full-jitter, and advanced teams can provide a custom backoff function.
Margo: SGTM. will PR readme, tests, and CHANGELOG entries.
Jess: timeline?
Hao: Node PR this week (WIP).
Margo: Python + sampleapp next week.
Sam: I’ll add the CI job & integration harness today.
Jess: perfect — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
